claim: The docstring asserts that because requests and streamed responses are awaited, a slow model call yields the event loop, and that a synchronous client here would stall every other request the server handles until it returned.
source_excerpt:
The client is the SDK's async client. Requests and streamed responses are
    awaited, so a slow model call yields the event loop; a synchronous client
    here would stall every other request the server handles until it returned.
verify_against: Every call site on this class that touches the SDK client, and any remaining blocking work on the request path
verify_hint: Check all `self._client` uses in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py` (`send_request`, `stream_request`) and whether any synchronous helper (e.g. token counting, retries, client construction) still runs inline on the loop; a falsifying input is a model call made through a code path that does not await the SDK

claim: `effective_row_cap(self._max_rows)` evaluated in the coroutine before `asyncio.to_thread` yields the same cap the per-request profile would give, and no other per-request context value (read-only profile, RLS settings) consumed inside `_run_sql_blocking` needs the same pre-read.
verify_against: The per-request profile context source of truth
